description: GENERIC worktree-policy — Universal baseline transplanted by transplant-bundle (git-worktree-isolation) to .claude/config/worktree-policy.json of target projects. Unlike brief2dev's internal policy (.claude/config/worktree-policy.json which includes brief2dev-specific tier1 paths like .brief2dev/**, output/**), this generic policy marks only cross-project git-ignored runtime directories and settings.json (for hook registration codegen) as Tier 1 (direct edit permitted). 100% Worktree Paradigm remains identical: all other git-tracked assets are Tier 3 (worktree enforced) and blocked by worktree-policy-guard when edited directly on protected branches (including README.md and .claude/config/**). External projects customize tier1 patterns to match their git-ignored output directories and protected_branches to match their default branch name.

tier1_main_allowed.description: Direct Edit/Write permitted on main branch — limited to git-ignored runtime/build artifacts and settings.json (for hook registration codegen). Project owners can customize output paths.

escape_hatch.description: Emergency bypass for urgent hotfixes or when hook/worktree infrastructure itself is broken

trunk_bash_allowlist.description: Opt-in. When enabled, worktree-policy-guard denies Bash commands on a protected branch unless every simple command matches one pattern. Each pattern is a regex source, anchored by the guard as ^(?:pattern)(?=\s|$), judged per command after env assignments, reserved words, wrappers (env/sudo/command/time/xargs ...) and git global options are removed. Commands in $( ), backticks and unquoted-delimiter heredoc bodies are judged too. Exempt: cd, and a command whose effective directory (cwd after an &&-chained cd, then cumulative git -C / make -C) is inside an existing linked worktree under .worktrees/ and none of whose path arguments or redirect targets reaches the trunk checkout or fails to resolve; after ; || | & a preceding cd no longer exempts. env -C <dir> counts as a cd; directories and paths are compared after realpath; a path word with .. plus brace/glob characters is unresolvable. Denied regardless: an output redirect into a file (anything but /dev/null or an fd), time -o <file>, any GIT_*= or CDPATH= assignment, and env -S '<cmd>'. Not enforced: file-writing options of a listed command (find -delete, git log --output=f) - exclude them in the pattern. A command that cannot be parsed (nesting deeper than 64) is denied. Requires worktree-policy-guard registered on the Bash matcher (see _adapt.opt_in_wiring).

_adapt.enforce_worktree_all_branches: false (default): only protected_branches are trunk. true: a non-worktree checkout on any branch except the escape_hatch.branch_patterns ones (hotfix/*) is treated like trunk, for git-flow repos that keep develop / release/* beside main. Then worktree-policy-guard denies tracked-file edits there (trunk_bash_allowlist, if enabled, applies there too), commit-guard denies git commit there, trunk-start-warning warns at session start, and worktree-shipping-guard never treats that checkout as a ship candidate; a root hotfix/* checkout may both edit and commit. Worktrees must live under .worktrees/ (make wt.new puts them there): that is what the guards recognise, so a linked worktree created elsewhere is blocked like the root checkout and its sessions get the start warning. Read by .cli/lib/trunk-branch.mjs#enforcesWorktreeOnAllBranches only; no registration change needed.
_adapt.trunk_ref_guard: true (default): the reference-transaction hook (.claude/scripts/trunk-ref-guard.mjs, self-installed by commit-guard) denies an AI session moving a protected branch to a commit absent from the remote-tracking refs, on every git path (commit / merge / cherry-pick / reset / update-ref; --no-verify does not skip it), except under a /create-pr lease. false: commit-guard does not install the hook (a repo's own reference-transaction hook stays untouched and unreported) and an already-installed one passes everything, for repos whose documented landing is an AI-run local merge into trunk (no remote, no lease). Only a JSON false opts out; a missing key or any other value keeps the guard on.
_adapt.session_owner_scope: "commit" (default): worktree-session-owner-guard checks git commit only. "all_bash": every Bash command is checked against every worktree it touches. Where it runs (cwd, each cd, cumulative git -C / make -C) gets Layer 1 (cross-worktree) and Layer 2 (live foreign lease); path arguments and redirect targets that resolve into a worktree (relative ../other paths included) get Layer 2 only. all_bash never claims, renews or adopts a lease for a non-commit command, so reading a worktree cannot take it over. An unparsable command is denied. Requires the guard's Bash registration without if: Bash(git *) (see opt_in_wiring).
_adapt.opt_in_wiring: The bundle registers both Bash hooks narrowly so non-opted-in targets pay no extra process per Bash call. To opt in under Claude Code, in .claude/settings.json PreToolUse matcher Bash: add worktree-policy-guard.mjs (no if) and remove the if from worktree-session-owner-guard.mjs. Re-transplanting keeps these edits (settings merge dedupes by command). Codex/Antigravity registrations already cover every Bash call.
_adapt.purpose: External project adaptation guide (the guard does not read this key — guidance only).
_adapt.how: Add your project's git-ignored output directories (refer to .gitignore) to tier1_main_allowed.patterns. Git-tracked source/configuration files (including this policy file itself) remain Tier 3 (worktree enforced) with settings.json as a codegen exception.
_adapt.disable: If worktree isolation is unneeded, simply omit worktree-policy-guard from settings.json/hook-registry.
_adapt.trunk_bash_allowlist_limits: Threat model: an honest agent that over-generalises, not a malicious one - a static allowlist cannot fence a shell completely. Opaque to the guard: interpreter payloads and scripts (bash -c, node -e, python -c, ./x.sh), write-by-argument tools (dd of=), allowlisted tools that execute project config (make targets, cargo build scripts), and an inherited CDPATH set outside the command. Keep such commands off the allowlist, and exclude file-writing options of listed commands in the pattern (negative lookahead: git log --output, git diff --ext-diff, git grep -O, make -f, cargo clippy --fix).
